compute.note: parameters = Nsite^2 + alpha + 2 + 2 alpha Nsite = 64^2 + 4 + 2 + 2*4*64 = 4614 COMPLEX parameters (ComplexType 1 in every def file; 9228 real numbers): pair-product orbitals f_ij without sublattice structure (NOrbitalIdx = Nsite^2), RBM hidden biases (alpha), physical-layer biases (2, one per spin), and translation-invariant RBM weights (2 alpha Nsite, the 1x1 RBM sublattice sub_rbm_phidx.py generates, as the method string states). samples = NVMCSample x MPI processes / NSplitSize = 100 x 8 / 1 = 800 per SR step: with NSplitSize = 1 every rank is its own sampling group (vmcmain.c "group1 = rank0/NSplitSize"), draws NVMCSample samples after NVMCWarmUp = 100 (each separated by NVMCInterval x Nsite = 64 proposals) and WeightAverageWE sums the weights over all ranks (average.c); iterations = NSROptItrStep = 1000 SR steps (the parameters are averaged over the last NSROptItrSmp = 100). All of these are the defaults of make_modpara, not overridden by the optimisation call. Each amplitude sums a Pfaffian of the 64-electron pair-product state over NSPGaussLeg x |NMPTrans| = 8 x 64 = 512 spin/momentum projection points. Doubt (why confidence is low): the script is the simplified template of programs/mVMC_makedef/README.txt ("For simplicity, we focus on the case of Ns=8x8"). It runs ONE optimisation stage with the projections and the RBM on from the start, while the README's protocol has three optimisation stages (f_ij alone from the UHF solution, then the RBM, then the projections) whose step counts are not stated anywhere, and it never runs the Lanczos step the energy includes: make_all.py also writes namelist_aft.def/modpara_aft.def (NVMCCalMode=1, NLanczosMode=1, NVMCWarmUp=500, NVMCInterval=5, NVMCSample=5000, NDataQtySmp=10) but mVMC.sh does not call it. So the counts are the script's single stage, not the published run's total. No time is recorded anywhere; "mpiexec -np 8" names MPI processes, not hardware.

compute.note: parameters = np = iesm + iesd + iesh + (iback(1..4)) + iesfree + iessw + iesup + ieskin = 13 + 14 + 0 + 4 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 0 = 32 variational parameters (the code's own formula, Main_uniform_wf.f), matching the 32 optimised values listed in datprep.d after the namelists (Jastrow, backflow, pairing/field and chemical-potential terms, in the order the code reads them; &nelectrons nelup=32 neldo=32; one determinant of backflow orbitals per configuration). The script does NOT optimise: datasvmc.d sets itestr=2 ("VMC", measurement with the fixed parameters read from datprep.d; itestr=-2 is the minimiser) and the program README says the input files contain "the optimal variational parameters". The run it scripts is one measurement of ngen = 2000000 Monte Carlo generations of nbra = 64 = N single-electron proposals each (one walker, nw=1), from which Energy.x takes bins of 1000 and drops the first 5. The &optimization namelist in the same file (nweight=5000 generations per SR step, ibinit=50, tau=0.02) is not read at itestr=2, and no file states how many optimisation steps produced the parameters, so samples and iterations (per optimisation step, and optimisation steps) are null. Doubt: the Fortran as committed is compiled for nx=45, L=270 (Main_uniform_wf.f parameter statement), so for this 64-site instance the program must be edited and recompiled before the script can run. compute.reported_as: We typically choose tau = 0.01 in this work, with which we have verified that the Trotter error is below the targeted statistical errors. || In this section, we present results at half-filling. As mentioned, the AFQMC results are numerically exact, as the sign problem is absent because of the particle-hole symmetry. We use a combination of the path-integral approach [40] and the random walk approach [25]. || In this work, we use a special form of the generalized Hartree-Fock (GHF) [34] wave function as TWF in the AFQMC calculations. This will increase the computation time by a factor of 2 to 4 in different portions of algorithm, because now the Slater determinant of up and down spin are coupled. || Earlier calculations were carried out at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Most of the calculations were carried out at the Extreme Science and Engineering Discovery Environment (XSEDE), which is supported by National Science Foundation Grant No. ACI-1053575, and the computational facilities at the College of William and Mary.
compute.source: Sec. II B (Trotter step); Sec. IV Results at half filling; Sec. III B (GHF trial wave function); Acknowledgments; energies from Appendix Table IV, arXiv:1605.09421 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Half-filling AFQMC data of Appendix Table IV (PBC and PBC-APBC, 4x4 to 16x16, U = 2-8). No walker counts, projection times, sample/block counts, core counts, core-hours or wall-clock are stated anywhere for these runs; the only quantitative method setting is the Trotter step tau = 0.01 (with a tau -> 0 extrapolation used only for the TABC data). The GHF trial-wave-function remark is a relative cost (factor 2-4 in computation time), not an absolute one.
